name: RSRS High-on-Low Regression Beta
note: An ordinary least squares fit of the bar HIGH on the bar LOW over the last reg_n bars -- the two series regressed against each other rather than against time or against price. Beta is how far the ceiling extends per unit the floor extends: large means buyers are winning the range, small means the high is capped while the low keeps sliding. Raw beta drifts with the instrument, so it is standardised against its own trailing z_n distribution, and z is multiplied by the regression R-squared (use_r2) so a reading taken from a noisy high/low relationship is discounted rather than trusted. Long on a cross up through s_in, short on a cross down through -s_in, out through s_out. Computed with offset prefix sums so the 18-bar cross-products stay numerically clean on a $700 index.

def family_init(ctx):
    import math
    bars = ctx.bars
    n = len(bars)
    N = max(4, int(ctx.p.reg_n))
    M = max(30, int(ctx.p.z_n))
    use_r2 = int(ctx.p.use_r2)

    base = float(bars[0]["c"])
    x = [float(b["l"]) - base for b in bars]      # the offset keeps the
    y = [float(b["h"]) - base for b in bars]      # cross-products conditioned

    sx = [0.0] * (n + 1)
    sy = [0.0] * (n + 1)
    sxx = [0.0] * (n + 1)
    sxy = [0.0] * (n + 1)
    syy = [0.0] * (n + 1)
    for i in range(n):
        sx[i + 1] = sx[i] + x[i]
        sy[i + 1] = sy[i] + y[i]
        sxx[i + 1] = sxx[i] + x[i] * x[i]
        sxy[i + 1] = sxy[i] + x[i] * y[i]
        syy[i + 1] = syy[i] + y[i] * y[i]

    beta = [None] * n
    r2 = [0.0] * n
    for i in range(N - 1, n):
        j = i + 1 - N
        mx = (sx[i + 1] - sx[j]) / N
        my = (sy[i + 1] - sy[j]) / N
        cxx = (sxx[i + 1] - sxx[j]) - N * mx * mx
        cxy = (sxy[i + 1] - sxy[j]) - N * mx * my
        cyy = (syy[i + 1] - syy[j]) - N * my * my
        if cxx <= 1e-12:
            continue
        beta[i] = cxy / cxx
        if cyy > 1e-12:
            v = (cxy * cxy) / (cxx * cyy)
            r2[i] = 0.0 if v < 0.0 else (1.0 if v > 1.0 else v)

    # z of beta against its own trailing M readings
    vals = []
    idx = []
    for i in range(n):
        if beta[i] is not None:
            vals.append(beta[i])
            idx.append(i)
    m = len(vals)
    ps = [0.0] * (m + 1)
    p2 = [0.0] * (m + 1)
    for k in range(m):
        ps[k + 1] = ps[k] + vals[k]
        p2[k + 1] = p2[k] + vals[k] * vals[k]
    zw = [None] * n
    for k in range(m):
        if k + 1 < M:
            continue
        mu = (ps[k + 1] - ps[k + 1 - M]) / M
        var = (p2[k + 1] - p2[k + 1 - M]) / M - mu * mu
        if var <= 1e-18:
            continue
        z = (vals[k] - mu) / math.sqrt(var)
        i = idx[k]
        zw[i] = z * r2[i] if use_r2 else z

    ctx.zw = ctx.series(zw, "rsrs_z")


def signal(ctx, i):
    z = ctx.zw[i]
    p = ctx.zw[i - 1]
    if z is None or p is None:
        return 0
    s = float(ctx.p.s_in)
    if p <= s and z > s:
        return 1
    if p >= -s and z < -s:
        return -1
    return 0


def exit_signal(ctx, i):
    """Support stopped winning: the standardised slope is back through neutral."""
    z = ctx.zw[i]
    if z is None or not ctx.positions:
        return False
    out = float(ctx.p.s_out)
    if ctx.positions[0]["side"] == "long":
        return z < out
    return z > -out
